findings.text: Forward-looking (out of scope for 1212, flag for the WARP-1208 live driver): freshness is a lexicographic ISO string compare (now > exp), correct only for fixed-width identical formats. A future live caller supplying now and expires_at in mismatched ISO representations (differing precision, or +00:00 vs Z) could misjudge freshness, a theoretical fail-OPEN WHEN a clock is present. WARP-1212 neither introduces nor worsens this (it only changes the no-clock branch) and it cannot cause a no-clock fail-open. Recommend the live driver normalize/assert a canonical fixed-width UTC Z format for both operands.

Observation, not a gap: KEY 2's no-clock fail-closed branch is not independently reachable through the full gate because KEY 1's _expired fires first when now is None; the KEY 2 hardening is proven at the shared _expired helper (selftest asserts _expired(conf-shaped, None) is True), sound since both keys use one helper with identical logic and KEY 1 already fails closed. No fail-open; KEY 2 coverage is helper-level, KEY 1 gate-level.
